title: Raga Devgandhari
hook: a short raga where a Guru admits the mind won't listen

segments.voice: Yesterday, a hymn in Gujri, the crane and her chicks, and your line was devotion in gujri. When your mind started scheming, did you ask it, why, mind? Day one thousand seventy-six.

This mind won't do a thing I tell it. I've taught it and taught it, and it won't turn from its bad thinking. In plain English, that's how a hymn of Guru Tegh Bahadur begins in the Guru Granth Sahib. No thunder, no threat. Just a tired, honest sentence about the mind, the kind someone might say to a friend after a long week of trying and failing to change a habit. It sits in a small section of the Granth, a raga set between bigger ones. Today: Raga Devgandhari.
screen: `THIS MIND WON'T LISTEN.` → `AN HONEST, TIRED SENTENCE.` → `RAGA DEVGANDHARI.`

segments.voice: Devgandhari is a short section. Turn the pages and it's over quickly, compared with the long sweeps of Gauri and Asa we've just walked through. Its mood is usually described as gentle and restrained. Not grand, not stormy. A soft voice in a quiet room. The hymns here come from Gurus, among them Guru Tegh Bahadur, and his are the ones we'll stay with. Back to that opening. The hymn goes on to describe the mind plainly: drunk on the world, it fills its own belly and forgets the Lord's praise. Like a dog's tail, it says, it won't be straightened. That's blunt. But listen to the tone. A Guru is speaking about the mind the way a tired parent talks about a stubborn child. There's no threat in it. There's no shouting. There's a plain admission that the work is slow, and then the work goes on. The last line turns: Nanak says, remember the Name every day, and the task will be done. That's what a gentle raga is for. Restraint isn't weakness. It's what lets a hard truth be heard without anyone flinching. If the words were sung in a fierce raga, they might sound like a scolding. Sung in Devgandhari, they sound like company. Trying to change and slipping back is an old story. The Granth doesn't pretend it doesn't happen. It meets it softly, and keeps going. So today's line is one word: gentle. Gentle toward the stubborn mind, and gentle in the way the truth is told.
screen: `A SHORT SECTION, A SOFT VOICE.` · `THIS MIND WON'T HEED A WORD.` · `LIKE A DOG'S TAIL, IT WON'T STRAIGHTEN.` · `RESTRAINT LETS TRUTH BE HEARD.` · then, large: `GENTLE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: speak to your own mind gently. Sit, and let your breath find its own pace. Bring to mind one habit you keep meaning to change and keep not changing. Notice the voice that usually comes with it, the harsh one. Now try a different tone, the tone of the hymn: tired maybe, honest, but kind. You might simply say, not yet, and that's where we are. Then let it go and rest. If you pray, you can say Waheguru softly, once, and leave the habit there. If you don't, let the kindness be the whole practice. Later, play a Devgandhari shabad, and notice how quiet it stays. The bell holds the time.
Raga Devgandhari. A short section of the Granth, gentle and restrained, where Guru Tegh Bahadur speaks honestly about a mind that won't listen. Today's word.
Your line: gentle. Today, when you slip on something you're trying to change, answer yourself the way you'd answer a friend who slipped. Day one thousand seventy-six.
